statement: In wild-type mouse L2/3 auditory-cortex pyramidal neurons (P28-P42, 34 C, synapses intact, K-gluconate pipette) 60 uM Ba2+ raised input resistance about 30 percent (172.7 to about 224 Mohm) with only a 1.5 mV depolarisation, an implied Ba2+-sensitive share of about 23 percent of the resting input conductance (percent derived by the producer from printed means).

The Ba2+-sensitive current of those neurons at -130 mV was -218 pA (60 percent block) and reversed at -89.6 mV on the recorded scale, which is within about 1 mV of a K+ equilibrium near -106 mV once the stated 16.2 mV calculated junction offset is removed (E_K and the offset arithmetic are the producer's, not a statement of the source), so a K+ current is a coherent reading and the offset is roughly 16 mV for that solution pair.

statement: Block of Kv7 with 5 uM XE-991 did not change resting potential (-83.4 to -82.4 mV) or the slope resistance near rest in adult rat L2/3 neurons (sharp electrode, 34 C), whose Kv7 current begins to activate near -70 mV; at a rest near -80 mV the Kv7 share was therefore small in that preparation (adult, not juvenile).

statement: Genetic loss of KCNQ2 raised input resistance 25 percent (239 to 299 Mohm) in L2/3 somatosensory pyramidal neurons at P15-P20 with synaptic blockers at room temperature and a resting potential near -67 mV on the corrected scale, an implied lost share of about 20 percent of the resting conductance when the cell rests there (RMP change not significant).

statement: XE-991 at 10 uM had no effect on recombinant Kv7.2 held at -70 mV and half-inhibits near -51 mV (CHO cells, room temperature), so an absent XE-991 effect on resting potential or resistance near -80 mV is expected whatever the Kv7 share and cannot be read as a small share.

statement: Block of Ih with 10 uM ZD7288 changed wild-type L2/3 auditory-cortex Rin by about +6 percent (+8 Mohm) and hyperpolarised the cell 4.7 mV, so Ih carried an order of 6 percent of the resting input conductance in those neurons (percent derived from a panel read-off baseline), not 28 percent.

In deep-layer (V-VI) mouse prefrontal neurons at P19-P25, ZD7288 at 50 uM raised the slope resistance at -80 mV from a median 55 to 244 Mohm ('data not shown') and hyperpolarised the cell 5 mV, so Ih can carry most of the conductance at -80 mV in deep neurons; this is not shown for L2/3 neurons, in which layer-3 neurons showed no prominent sag at P7-P28 in another dataset.

statement: No source was found in which a K2P tool (TASK, TREK or TRAAK blocker, opener or knockout) was applied to neocortical pyramidal neurons with input resistance and resting potential reported, within PubMed (MCP tool) and Europe PMC searches of 2026-11-10 (queries Q11-Q17, Q22); the only K2P-related items read were mRNA detection (KCNK3, KCNK9) and a modelled leak in deep-layer neurons.

From P7 to P28 layer-3 pyramidal input resistance falls about 47 percent per interval (405.9 to 213.4 to 110.3 Mohm) and rest moves -61.6 to -70.0 to -73.0 mV in mouse prelimbic cortex (31 C, K-gluconate), so P13-P17 sits mid-transition, and the P14 value is about twice the Wwox wild-type 103 Mohm (different area, layer and method).

statement: A K+ gain model (Fmr1 knockout, L2/3 auditory cortex) shows the opposite pattern to Wwox: Rin 172.7 to 124.5 Mohm, rest -78.3 to -82.0 mV, Ba2+-sensitive current -218 to -307 pA at -130 mV; listed as an external calibration for a K+ conductance change of known sign (preprint).

A measured junction potential of -10 mV (to be added to recorded voltages) was reported for a 114 K-gluconate and 6 KCl pipette solution against an ACSF of 125 NaCl, 3.5 KCl, 0.5 MgCl2, 1 CaCl2 in mouse L2/3 neurons at room temperature; the Wwox composition differs (135 K-gluconate, 10 NaCl, 1 MgCl2, 2 Na2ATP internal; 123 NaCl, 3.5 KCl, 1.3 MgSO4, 1.5 CaCl2, 25 NaHCO3 bath; 35 C) and its junction potential was not measured.

statement: Taken together the Ba2+-sensitive share (about 23 percent, WT L2/3, P28-P42) and the KCNQ2-dependent share when the cell rests near -67 mV (about 20 percent, P15-P20) are each of the order of the 28 percent lost conductance implied by the Wwox table, while the ZD7288-sensitive share is about 6 percent; no source tests whether any of these currents is smaller in Wwox-deficient neurons (a blocker effect shows that a current contributes, not that it is altered).
